definitions.explanation: Not detailed or precise; giving only a general outline or approximation. Used for plans, estimates, descriptions, and explanations that omit fine details.

examples.japanese: {大|おお}まかな{計画|けいかく}を{立|た}てた。
{大|おお}まかな{流|なが}れを{説明|せつめい}してください。
まずは{大|おお}まかな{見積|みつ}もりを{出|だ}して、{詳細|しょうさい}は{後|あと}で{詰|つ}めましょう。
examples.english: Let's first produce a rough estimate and work out the details later.

notes:
USAGE:
Used as a na-adjective modifier ({大|おお}まかな + noun) or adverbially ({大|おお}まかに). Very common in business and everyday conversation when discussing plans, summaries, or approximations.

FORMS:
- Modifier: {大|おお}まかな{計画|けいかく} (a rough plan)
- Adverbial: {大|おお}まかに{言|い}えば (roughly speaking)
- Predicate: {説明|せつめい}が{大|おお}まかだ (the explanation is rough)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {大|おお}まかな{見積|みつ}もり (rough estimate)
- {大|おお}まかな{流|なが}れ (general flow)
- {大|おお}まかな{内容|ないよう} (general content)
- {大|おお}まかに{分|わ}ける (to divide broadly)
